chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the tooth-brushing for the fasting person, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, he may brush his teeth at any time of the day he desires.'

key_terms.السِّوَاكِ: The act of brushing teeth with a siwak twig

ai.seo_question: Does using siwak break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that using the siwak does not break the fast, addressing early juristic debates on whether the act constitutes 'eating or drinking.' The phrase 'any part of the day' (*ayya an-nahar shi'a*) emphasizes the general permissibility throughout daylight hours, though later scholars often preferred morning usage to maximize the Sunnah's reward before Dhuhr. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining ritual purity (taharah) and preserving the integrity of the fast in Shia fiqh.
